summary: Steel Blaw-Knox tower moved from Snow Hill in 1935 and removed in 1975; a 2004 survey-mark page found only concrete footings left on the summit.

facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1975; the survey-enthusiast page reports only concrete footings remain

events.note: Unimproved bald-top observation point listed under the Dancing Ridge name: used circa 1917 (statewide list), established prior to 1918 (regional listing); neither list says whether it is this site, so the story does not link it to the summit or the steel tower
Steel tower moved from Snow Hill and renamed Dancing Ridge; the Dancing Ridge register says it was constructed in 1935
Tower removed; the register and the statewide list both give 1975
Survey station on the summit recovered in destroyed condition on June 17, 2004; only concrete footings reported
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 16, 2008

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Dancing Ridge register says the steel tower was constructed in 1935; the Snow Hill register says it was moved in 1935. The story reports the move and quotes both wordings; it does not state a construction year.
The 1975 removal date is given by two sources and is used. The 2000 photo caption 'Tower remains in 2000' is left unexplained because the register does not say what it shows.

notes_for_editor: The record already holds the 2000 Pete Carron photo; no new photos were added. Source 5 is a hobbyist survey page, not an official source. Its NGS notes say photographs were not submitted, while the page says they were, so check NGS datasheet LY2684 before relying on the 'destroyed' status. The statewide list has two Dancing Ridge rows: a bald site used circa 1917 and this steel tower. The bald row may refer to this site or to Dancing Ridge Tower Site I (US 262); this was not resolved. The register and the Snow Hill entry disagree on whether 1935 was construction or the move. Staffing, fires, access and visitor rules are not in any source read.
